exposure: antenatal radiotherapy (for a subset of patients)
outcome: obstetric complications (preterm contractions, preterm rupture of membranes)
admission to neonatal intensive care unit (NICU)
cohort: The study included 134 pregnant patients diagnosed with Hodgkin lymphoma and 211 non-pregnant matched controls for maternal survival analyses.
finding: Neonates prenatally exposed to chemotherapy had lower birthweight percentiles, and their mothers experienced more obstetric complications like preterm contractions and preterm rupture of membranes, but maternal survival for Hodgkin lymphoma was comparable between pregnant and non-pregnant patients.
country: Belgium, Czech Republic, Denmark, Greece, Israel, Italy, Mexico, the Netherlands, Russia, the UK, USA
birth_weight: N/A (birthweight percentiles were measured as an outcome for neonates, not an inclusion criterion for the study population)
gest_age: N/A (incidence of small for gestational age was measured as an outcome for neonates, not an inclusion criterion for the study population)
